question: Does the artifact a customer receives carry the probe's own measured error rate, and does the direction it is wrong in pay the operator?

method.scope: structural — a declared coverage constant rendered into the artifact
method.direction: lexical over a narrow accuracy vocabulary, every match quoted
method.rate: numeric — the committed figure, citation verified on every run

rubric.rule: The artifact does not carry an accuracy figure — either the number is committed elsewhere in the repository and omitted here, or it was never measured. A customer cannot discount a record whose error rate they cannot see.
The artifact does not say which way the tool is wrong. Scope disclosure does not substitute: knowing what was looked at says nothing about whether what came back is right.

The undisclosed error direction is the one that increases the operator's revenue, judged against the revenue model the candidate write-up states. Conditional on the direction being undisclosed: an operator who names the way its own errors pay it has disclosed the conflict, which is the whole mitigation this deduction exists to ask for.

direction_evidence: **Accuracy (precision 0.821–0.881, recall 0.975):** this list both over- and under-reports.
That is why the precision figure is printed here, beside the findings it applies to, rather than supplied on request.
**Precision 0.821–0.881** (over-reporting — this engine lists defects that are not defects), measured 2026-08-21 on 118 built pages across 7 applications, 67 findings reviewed one by one.

- Why it is not the last word: That denominator excluded colour contrast (1.4.3) entirely — the review predates this engine's contrast rule, so the figure describes the non-contrast findings and no contrast finding has been precision-checked.

**Recall 0.975** (under-reporting — this engine misses defects that are real), measured 2026-08-21 on the same 118 pages, compared against axe-core 4.13.0 over the 13 success criteria either engine declares automated or partial.
"accuracy_statement": "Both numbers below were measured on this portfolio's own built pages, not on your site, and they describe this engine rather than the audit you are buying.

"caveat": "That denominator excluded colour contrast (1.4.3) entirely \u2014 the review predates this engine's contrast rule, so the figure describes the non-contrast findings and no contrast finding has been precision-checked.

rate_committed.reads: 12–18% of the findings in the list a customer is handed are not defects

disclosure.revenue_model: €900–€1,800 fixed-price job per shop, €49–€99/month retainer after (candidates/eaa-remediation-pipeline.md)

direction_evidence: False positives are expected; a suppressed finding that should not have been is the failure this tool is built to avoid, and both are possible.
disclosure.rate_absent_because: The direction this tool's own record calls "the failure this tool is built to avoid" — a suppression that should not have happened — has never been measured. validation-2026-08-21-build-surface.json records suppression *rates*, which say how much was suppressed and nothing about how much of that was wrong.

direction_evidence: **Accuracy (detection rate 6 of 17 (0.35), detection latency 110 days (median)):** this watch misses most dormancy and reports late.
"accuracy_statement": "These figures come from replaying this watch over the recorded history of the mirrors it follows, holding each source out in turn.

rate_committed.quote: episodes (0.35) at a median latency of 110 days
rate_committed.reads: roughly two thirds of the dormancy episodes the customer is paying to be told about are not detected

direction_evidence: Measured against 34 synthetic fixture cases in this probe's own test suite (author-authored to isolate each rule, not an independent or held-out corpus): 0 false positives, 0 false negatives on the 16/34 positive-rule opportunities those fixtures cover across all seven rules (R1-R7).
This is a floor on precision and recall, not an out-of-sample estimate: every fixture was written already knowing which rule it was meant to trip.
**Zero false positives is a design property confirmed, not guaranteed.

That is why zero false positives held on every fixture built to test it -- it is what the design predicts -- but 34 author-authored fixtures confirm the design on the cases it was built for, not on production workflow files this probe has never seen.
**False negatives on attack classes none of the seven rules encode are real and unmeasured.

R5 and R6 are posture records, not defect calls, so a false positive there would not mean "wrongly flagged an attacker path" the way it would for R1-R4 or R7; they are included in the count above on the narrower, honest claim that each fires exactly when its own documented structural condition is present, which is the only accuracy claim posture rules admit.

rate_committed.quote: 0 false positives, 0 false negatives on the 16/34 positive-rule opportunities
rate_committed.reads: 0 false positives and 0 false negatives on 34 author-authored synthetic fixture cases (16 positive-rule opportunities) across all seven rules — a floor on precision/recall on cases designed to exercise the rules that exist, not an out-of-sample estimate and not a measurement of attack classes none of the seven rules encodes.

disclosure.measured_error_direction: false negatives on attack/misconfiguration classes outside R1-R7 (unmeasured, and structurally unmeasurable by this fixture corpus); zero false positives measured on the 34-case fixture corpus, not independently or out-of-sample validated

scoring.alignment_reasoning: The audit is the qualification step that sells the fixed-price job, so a finding list inflated by 12–18% converts better. a11y-own-sites reached the same point from the other side: "a free qualification audit therefore needs a build-artifact filter before a stranger reads it."

The product's whole value proposition is cutting the customer's alert count. A suppression that should not have happened both improves the headline the subscription is sold on and is invisible to the subscriber.

Nuisance alarms cost the operator churn — the probe measures 43 alarm-days per source-year at the high-recall setting — while a missed dormancy episode costs nothing and cannot be observed by the customer, who sees silence either way. The cheapest tuning is the one that fails them.
The write-up states no revenue model, so there is nothing to align against. Not scored either way rather than assumed benign.
